instruction: Archive all files in the "/tmp/test_files" directory tree that were last modified 30 days ago into a tar.gz file

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

result.command: bash -c 'if find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name "*.tar.gz" -type f | grep -q .; then if tar -tzf $(find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name "*.tar.gz" -type f | head -1) 2>/dev/null | grep -q "old_file"; then echo "Success: Old files archived"; else echo "Fail: Archive does not contain old files"; fi; else echo "Fail: No tar.gz archive found"; fi'

metadata.explanation: Task requires archiving files modified 30 days ago into a tar.gz file. Uses command-line verification to check if a tar.gz archive exists in /tmp and contains the old files. No custom functions needed - reuses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Wrong search location: Command searches '/tmp -maxdepth 1' but instruction specifies files are in '/tmp/test_files' directory tree
Incomplete verification: Only checks if archive contains a file with 'old_file' string, doesn't verify files were actually modified 30 days ago
Missing completeness check: Doesn't verify ALL matching files were archived (partial archiving would pass)
Hardcoded string dependency: Relies on 'old_file' naming pattern from setup.sh, not mentioned in instruction
No source path verification: Doesn't verify archived files came from /tmp/test_files specifically
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change search location from '/tmp -maxdepth 1' to '/tmp/test_files' to match instruction
Verify archive contains files from /tmp/test_files by checking tar contents paths
Add verification that archived files have modification time matching 30 days ago criterion
Count files in /tmp/test_files matching the 30-day criterion and verify same count in archive
Consider checking setup.sh to understand actual test file structure and modify verification accordingly
